cards.headline: Port St. Lucie's $30 Million Oak Hammock Flood Project Still Years Out
cards.teaser: After viral videos showed flooded streets near SW California Boulevard, city budget documents reveal a $30 million stormwater plan for the Oak Hammock area, funded partly by a proposed $6 assessment hike, though officials say construction remains years away.
cards.body:
Videos showing flooded roads and vehicles struggling through standing water in several Port St. Lucie neighborhoods have renewed attention on the city's stormwater spending, including a $30 million Oak Hammock Watershed Improvement Project that remains in its early planning stages. The city's proposed capital plan for fiscal years 2027 through 2031, submitted to City Council on April 13, includes $8 million in each of the first two years and $7 million in each of the next two for the project, paid for through stormwater bond financing. Part of that money would come from a proposed $6 increase in the annual stormwater assessment, raising it from $183 to $189, according to the city's website.

Port St. Lucie has received about 4 inches of rain over the past 48 hours, with another 2 to 4 inches possible by the end of the week. Frank Camarda, who has lived near SW California Boulevard and SW Plantation Terrace for more than 20 years, said Tuesday night's flooding turned his street into a detour as drivers tried to bypass flooded roads, including what he believes was Savona Boulevard. Camarda said he had not seen flooding on his own street before but has watched water pool near Oak Hammock a couple of times. He also said city crews used to clean the swale in front of his home about once a month, but he believes that has stopped. "I've been waiting for these guys to clean up. I haven't seen them," Camarda said.

City spokesperson Scott Samples said the rain came in too fast for the stormwater system to keep up, with canals, swales and retention ponds already full before the latest downpours hit. At one location the city monitored, he said, about two feet of water arrived in roughly 30 minutes. Samples said water had receded from most roadways by about 8:30 p.m. Tuesday, which he described as the system doing what it was designed to do. He said Public Works checks drainage before heavy rain and works to keep swales, drains and canals clear, but there is only so much crews can do when that much water arrives at once. He said residents who cannot get home should find another place to stay if possible, and that the city is working closely with police on safety.

Samples said the city has just begun early data analysis for Oak Hammock, which he placed in the California Boulevard area. That work will guide the design of a multi-phase project that could include new retention ponds, pumps for canals, or raising the roadway at California and Savona boulevards so water drains off. He said it is hard to predict when residents will see construction or a finished project because the city must first gather data, settle on a design and line up funding. "It will move as fast as it possibly can," Samples said. The project covers a large area east of Interstate 95, north of the C-23 Canal and Port St. Lucie Boulevard, and west of Florida's Turnpike. The stormwater assessment also helps fund four other projects, the Elkcam Basin, the E-8 Canal, Hogpen Slough, and faster replacement of swales and culverts, across a drainage system that includes about 200 miles of canals, 1,200 miles of swales and more than 6,000 culverts. The city notes that maintaining swales and driveway culverts between the edge of the pavement and the property line is the property owner's responsibility under city code.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Woman Shot At While Fleeing South Sixth Street Attack
cards.teaser: A woman escaped by car after being attacked and shot at during a domestic dispute on South Sixth Street in Fort Pierce. Two 18-year-olds now face attempted homicide and accessory charges.
cards.body:
A woman fled for her life on South Sixth Street in Fort Pierce after she was attacked and then shot at while driving away, according to the Fort Pierce Police Department. Two 18-year-olds have since been arrested in connection with the attack.

Police responded to South Sixth Street at 7:12 a.m. Saturday, October 3, after the victim called 911 to report that someone was shooting at her. Investigators determined the woman had gone to the address to speak with her boyfriend about their relationship. When she arrived, several people ran out of the residence and began attacking her.

The victim managed to break free, get into her vehicle, and drive away, police said. As she fled, one of the suspects grabbed a gun from the property and opened fire on her vehicle. A second person then allegedly drove the shooter away from the scene.

Police identified the suspects as Keibin Lopez-Godoy, 18, and Kailee Yurubi, 18. Lopez-Godoy faces a charge of first-degree attempted homicide, while Yurubi faces a charge of accessory after the fact.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Moves Precincts 39, 52 Polling Site for Nov. 3 Election
cards.teaser: Voters in two St. Lucie County precincts will cast ballots at a new location after renovations closed their usual polling place. Election officials are encouraging early voting to help ease the transition.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County voters assigned to Precincts 39 and 52 will vote at a temporary polling location for the Nov. 3 general election because of renovations at their regular site. Supervisor of Elections Gertrude Walker announced Tuesday that the two precincts will move from the Spanish Lakes Country Club clubhouse to Lakewood Park Church, 5405 Turnpike Feeder Road in Fort Pierce.

Walker encouraged affected voters, and voters countywide, to consider casting ballots early to avoid lines on Election Day. The county's newest early voting site, Lakewood Park Branch Library at 7605 Santa Barbara Drive in Fort Pierce, is now open for the first time for a general election. Other early voting locations include the Renaissance Business Park at 4132 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce, the Zora Neale Hurston Library at 3008 Avenue D in Fort Pierce, the MIDFlorida Credit Union Event Center at 9221 SE Event Center Place in Port St. Lucie, the Community Center at 2195 SE Airoso Blvd. in Port St. Lucie, the Lewis Library at 2950 Rosser Blvd. in Port St. Lucie, the Indian River State College Veterans Center of Excellence at 500 NW California Blvd. in Port St. Lucie, and Minsky Gym at 750 SW Darwin Blvd. in Port St. Lucie. Early voting runs daily until 6 p.m.

Voters who plan to cast a vote-by-mail ballot are reminded that a deadline applies to request one. Those returning ballots by mail are encouraged to do so at least seven days before Election Day to ensure timely delivery. Vote-by-mail ballots can also be dropped off in person at any early voting site or at designated Supervisor of Elections offices, including the Renaissance Business Park at 4132 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce, the St. Lucie West South County Annex at 250 NW Country Club Drive in Port St. Lucie, the Havert L. Fenn Center, and the Tradition Tax Collector office at 10264 SW Village Parkway.

Walker's office is urging residents in Precincts 39 and 52 to note the change ahead of time so they know where to go on Election Day. Voters with questions about their assigned precinct or early voting options can confirm details through the St. Lucie County Supervisor of Elections office.

hero.headline: Treasure Coast High Student Critical After SUV Hits Him on Way to School in PSL
hero.body:
A 14-year-old Treasure Coast High School student remains hospitalized in critical condition after being struck by an SUV while walking to school Wednesday morning in Port St. Lucie, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department. Investigators are now piecing together the circumstances of the crash, including a delay before the driver realized he had hit a person and returned to the scene.

Police said the crash happened around 6 a.m. near the intersection of Southwest Port St. Lucie Boulevard and Southwest Squirrel Avenue. The freshman was walking northbound along Port St. Lucie Boulevard on his way to school and was near the edge of the roadway alongside construction barrels when he was struck from behind by a 2002 Ford Excursion driven by a 72-year-old man.

According to police, the driver initially believed he had hit a construction barrel and did not realize he had struck a person. Authorities said he later made a U-turn at the next location where it was safe to do so and returned to the scene. Once back in the area, the driver activated his hazard lights and found the teen unconscious on the side of the roadway. Police said he immediately called 911 and has remained cooperative throughout the investigation. Investigators said there were no apparent signs of impairment involving the driver, though they noted the assessment is preliminary and could change as the investigation continues.

The student suffered life-threatening injuries and remains hospitalized in critical condition, according to police. The crash remains under investigation. Police are asking anyone who witnessed the incident or who may have dash camera, surveillance or other video footage from the area around the time of the crash to come forward. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Police Arrest Two After Woman Shot At Fleeing Attack
cards.teaser: A woman escaped an attack on South Sixth Street and was shot at as she drove away. Fort Pierce police have charged an 18-year-old with attempted homicide and another with accessory after the fact.
cards.body:
A woman was attacked and then shot at while fleeing in her vehicle after going to a South Sixth Street home to speak with her boyfriend about their relationship, according to the Fort Pierce Police Department. Officers responded to the scene at 7:12 a.m. on Saturday, October 3, after the victim called police to report that someone was shooting at her.

Police said the investigation found that when the woman arrived at the residence, several people ran outside and began attacking her. She managed to escape, get into her vehicle, and drive away. As she fled, one of the suspects grabbed a gun from the property and opened fire on her vehicle, according to police.

Fort Pierce police arrested two 18-year-olds in connection with the shooting. Keibin Lopez-Godoy faces a charge of first-degree attempted homicide for allegedly firing the gun at the victim as she drove off. Kailee Yurubi faces a charge of accessory after the fact for allegedly driving the shooter away from the scene.

The case remains under investigation by the Fort Pierce Police Department.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Flooding Puts Spotlight Back on $30 Million Oak Hammock Project
hero.body:
Flooding that covered roads and stranded vehicles across several Port St. Lucie neighborhoods this week is renewing scrutiny of the city's stormwater system, including a $30 million drainage project still in its early planning stages and a proposed $6 increase to the annual stormwater assessment. Port St. Lucie has received about 4 inches of rain over the past 48 hours, and another 2 to 4 inches could fall by the end of the week. City crews are monitoring conditions as water recedes, and officials are reminding drivers and pedestrians to stay out of flooded roads because it is difficult to judge how deep the water is.

Frank Camarda, who has lived near SW California Boulevard and SW Plantation Terrace for more than 20 years, said Tuesday night's flooding turned his street into a detour as drivers tried to bypass other flooded roads, including what he believes was Savona Boulevard. Camarda said he had never seen flooding on his own street before, though he has watched water pool near Oak Hammock on a couple of occasions. He also said city crews used to clean the swale in front of his home about once a month, and he believes that maintenance has stopped. "I've been waiting for these guys to clean up. I haven't seen them," Camarda said.

City spokesperson Scott Samples said the rain fell too fast for the stormwater system to keep up, with canals, swales and retention ponds already full before the storm hit. At one location the city monitored, he said, about two feet of water arrived in roughly 30 minutes. Samples said water had receded from most roadways by about 8:30 p.m. Tuesday, which he described as the stormwater system working as designed. He said Public Works checks drainage ahead of heavy rain and works to keep swales, drains and canals clear, but there is only so much crews can do when that much water arrives at once. He said residents who cannot get home should find another place to stay if possible, and that the city is coordinating with police on safety.

The city's proposed capital plan for fiscal years 2027 through 2031, submitted to City Council on April 13, includes the Oak Hammock Watershed Improvement Project, which covers a large area east of Interstate 95, north of the C-23 Canal and Port St. Lucie Boulevard, and west of Florida's Turnpike. The plan calls for $8 million in each of the first two years and $7 million in each of the following two, totaling $30 million, funded through stormwater bond financing, and would add new retention ponds, pump systems and upgraded valves. Samples said the city has only begun early data analysis for the project in the California Boulevard area, work that will guide a multi-phase design that could include new retention ponds, canal pumps or raising the roadway at California and Savona boulevards so water drains more effectively. He said it is hard to predict when construction will begin because the city must first gather data, finalize a design and secure funding, but he called Oak Hammock a city priority. "It will move as fast as it possibly can," Samples said. Part of the funding would come from a proposed $6 increase to the annual stormwater assessment, raising it from $183 to $189, which the city says would help pay for five flood-related projects: Oak Hammock, the Elkcam Basin, the E-8 Canal, Hogpen Slough, and faster replacement of swales and culverts. The city's drainage system includes about 200 miles of canals, 1,200 miles of swales and more than 6,000 culverts, and city code places responsibility for maintaining swales and driveway culverts, from the pavement edge to the property line, on individual property owners.

hero.body:
Fort Pierce Police have released new details on the shooting that erupted from a domestic dispute on South 6th Street over the weekend, confirming that a woman was attacked and then shot at as she drove away to escape. Keibin Lopez-Godoy, 18, faces a charge of first-degree attempted homicide, and Kailee Yurubi, 18, faces a charge of accessory after the fact, police said.

According to the Fort Pierce Police Department, officers responded to South 6th Street at 7:12 a.m. on Saturday, October 3, after the victim called 911 and reported that someone was shooting at her. Investigators said the woman had gone to the address to speak with her boyfriend about their relationship. When she arrived, several people ran out of the residence and attacked her, police said.

The victim managed to break away, get into her vehicle, and drive off, according to police. As she fled, one of the suspects grabbed a gun from the property and opened fire on her vehicle, police said. A second suspect was arrested for allegedly driving the shooter away from the scene afterward.

Lopez-Godoy and Yurubi were both taken into custody and identified by Fort Pierce Police in connection with the attack. Lopez-Godoy is charged with first-degree attempted homicide, while Yurubi is charged as an accessory after the fact.

cards.headline: Five Years Later, PSL Police Still Seek Answers in Gabriella Hanley Killing
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie detectives are still examining forensic and digital evidence five years after 20-year-old Gabriella Hanley was shot and killed on Southeast Green River Parkway. Investigators are asking anyone with information to come forward.
cards.body:
Five years after the shooting death of 20-year-old Gabriella Gina Hanley, the Port St. Lucie Police Department says it is still actively working the case and seeking answers. Officers responded to reports of multiple gunshots near Southeast Green River Parkway and Southeast Charleston Drive after Hanley was shot while driving south on Green River Parkway in a black Kia Forte with her boyfriend, Darrick Mincey Jr. Police said another vehicle pulled alongside them and fired multiple rounds into the car.

Officers and rescue personnel began life-saving measures after finding Hanley with multiple gunshot wounds. She was pronounced dead Oct. Mincey was also struck by gunfire but survived. Hanley left behind a 20-month-old baby at the time of her death.

Investigators found that the Kia had been struck by 37 bullet impacts. Numerous 9mm cartridge casings were recovered at the scene, and forensic evidence indicated the bullets were fired from two separate rifles, according to police. In 2022, investigators said they had identified three people of interest, but no charges have been filed against anyone in the case.

Five years after the shooting, Port St. Lucie detectives are continuing to conduct interviews, examine forensic evidence and review digital evidence as they work to bring the case to a resolution. Anyone with information is asked to call the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS (8477).

cards.headline: Fugitive Murder Suspect Returned to Indian River County Jail
cards.teaser: Michael Waggle, who fled after a fatal shooting, was captured in West Virginia and is now back in Indian River County, held without bail on a first-degree murder charge.
cards.body:
A man who fled Indian River County after a fatal shooting has been returned to the area and booked into the Indian River County Jail. Michael A. Waggle, 33, was booked into the jail on Monday, Oct. 5, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office jail database. He is charged with first-degree murder in the shooting death of Dawn M. Kriskewic.

The sheriff's office said Waggle and Kriskewic were in some sort of relationship at the time of the killing. After the shooting, Waggle fled the area and was later captured at a motel in Dunbar, West Virginia.

Court documents show Waggle was transferred to the Mecklenburg County Sheriff's Office in Charlotte, North Carolina, in September. Indian River County Sheriff's Office personnel traveled to the Mecklenburg County Sheriff's Office to retrieve Waggle and bring him back to Indian River County.

Waggle is now being held in the Indian River County Jail in Vero Beach without bail as he faces the first-degree murder charge.

hero.headline: UF Study Finds Dengue-Linked Mosquito Thriving in Indian River County Yards
hero.teaser: A UF/IFAS study in Vero Beach found surprisingly high numbers of Aedes aegypti, the mosquito most linked to dengue worldwide, in Indian River County backyards, though no locally acquired dengue cases have been reported in the county.
hero.body:
Researchers at UF/IFAS' Florida Medical Entomology Laboratory in Vero Beach have found unexpectedly high numbers of Aedes aegypti, the yellow fever mosquito and one of the two species most closely tied to dengue transmission worldwide, in residential yards across suburban Indian River County. The finding does not mean dengue is circulating in the county. No locally acquired dengue cases were listed for Indian River County in the Florida Department of Health's latest weekly surveillance report, which covers Sept. 20-26.

Researchers had expected yards in the area to be dominated by Aedes albopictus, also known as the Asian tiger mosquito. Instead they found relatively high numbers of Aedes aegypti, prompting new attention to backyard mosquito control and personal bite prevention, according to the researchers.

The first-of-its-kind study paired mosquito trapping at homes with a smartphone-based Bite Diary that allowed residents to record when and where they were bitten. Researchers collected 3,788 female mosquitoes from 78 yards. Of 70 reported bites, nearly 93% happened outdoors and nearly 74% happened at home, according to the peer-reviewed study. The number of mosquitoes trapped in a yard was not associated with how many bites residents reported. Instead, people who spent more time outside in the evening, between 5 p.m. and 9 p.m., reported more bites. Gardening and walking dogs were among the activities commonly reported when bites occurred.

The study comes during a record year for dengue in Florida. The state has reported nearly 500 cases in 2026, including 252 locally acquired infections and 245 travel-associated cases, according to the Department of Health's Sept. 20-26 surveillance report. Locally acquired cases were reported in Hillsborough, Miami-Dade, Orange, Palm Beach, Pasco, Pinellas and Polk counties, with Hillsborough County, the center of the state's outbreak, accounting for 223 of them. Palm Beach County had one locally acquired case and 12 travel-associated cases, while St. Lucie County had six travel-associated cases. State health officials also reported 20 mosquito pools testing positive for dengue statewide. Dengue spreads when an infected mosquito bites a person and does not pass directly between people. Symptoms can include fever, severe muscle and joint pain, rash, nausea and pain behind the eyes, and anyone with symptoms, especially after travel to an area where dengue is common, should contact a health care provider. Health officials urge residents to use EPA-registered insect repellent, wear long sleeves and pants when practical, repair window and door screens, and dump standing water from containers such as buckets, flowerpots, toys, tires and pool covers.

Researchers collected 3,788 female mosquitoes from 78 yards. Of 70 reported bites, nearly 93% happened outdoors and nearly 74% happened at home, according to the peer-reviewed study . The number of mosquitoes trapped in a yard was not associated with the number of bites residents reported. Instead, people who spent more time outside during the evening, from 5 p.m. to 9 p.m., reported more bites. Gardening and walking dogs were among activities commonly reported when bites occurred. Dengue is spread when an infected mosquito bites a person; it does not spread directly from person to person. Symptoms can include fever, severe muscle and joint pain, rash, nausea and pain behind the eyes. People with symptoms should contact a health care provider, especially after travel to an area where dengue is common. Health officials urge residents to use EPA-registered insect repellent, wear long sleeves and pants when practical, repair window and door screens, and dump standing water from containers such as buckets, flowerpots, toys, tires and pool covers.

cards.headline: New I-95 Oslo Road Interchange in Indian River County Opens Over a Year Early
cards.body:
A new $100 million I-95 interchange at Oslo Road in Indian River County has opened more than a year ahead of schedule, giving southern county residents their first new direct connection to the interstate in nearly 50 years. Governor Ron DeSantis traveled to Indian River County on Monday to mark the completion of the project, which state officials say will speed up emergency response, ease traffic congestion and improve freight movement for local businesses.

DeSantis said the interchange will ease pressure on nearby access points at Indrio Road and State Road 60 by giving drivers a new way onto I-95 directly from Oslo Road. He said motorists using that route can expect their travel times to I-95 to be cut roughly in half. State transportation officials project traffic along the corridor will keep growing through 2045. "This is going to bring a new critical connection to I-95 for a part of the state that has changed quite a bit," DeSantis said.

State officials say the interchange carries major public safety benefits for southern Indian River County. The state estimates emergency response times in the area could drop by as much as 56%, giving first responders faster access to crashes and other emergencies. "This will ultimately save some lives because time is of the essence in some of these situations," DeSantis said. Florida Department of Transportation Secretary Jared Perdue called the improved access for first responders one of the project's most important features. "Every single second counts when it comes to saving lives, and this is going to reduce the time it takes for first responders to get to incidents substantially," Perdue said. The new interchange is also expected to give trucks and commercial traffic a more direct route to the interstate, benefiting freight movement for businesses in southern Indian River County.

The project was accelerated through Florida's Moving Florida Forward initiative, a DeSantis administration program designed to speed up major road construction statewide. Perdue said FDOT used a "voluntary acceleration" approach that rewarded contractors for finishing work faster, allowing the Oslo Road interchange to open about 400 days ahead of schedule. As part of the project, FDOT also acquired nearby land to create a dedicated gopher tortoise habitat, which officials say will serve as the only relocation site of its kind in Southeast Florida for protected tortoises displaced by infrastructure work. The interchange is part of nearly $1 billion in planned transportation investments across the Treasure Coast. "This interchange sets a clear example of how Florida delivers infrastructure that improves quality of life today while building more capacity for the future," DeSantis said.

Waggle is facing a first-degree murder charge and is being held without bail in the Indian River County Jail in Vero Beach.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Flooding Spurs Scrutiny of $30 Million Oak Hammock Drainage Plan
hero.body:
Flooding this week left roads covered with water and vehicles struggling to pass through several Port St. Lucie neighborhoods, pushing the city's $30 million Oak Hammock drainage plan and a proposed stormwater fee increase into the spotlight. The city says it has received about 4 inches of rain over the past 48 hours, with another 2 to 4 inches possible by the end of the week. City crews are monitoring conditions as water recedes, and officials are warning drivers and pedestrians to stay out of flooded roads because it is hard to tell how deep the water is.

Frank Camarda, who has lived near SW California Boulevard and SW Plantation Terrace for more than 20 years, said Tuesday night's flooding turned his street into a detour as drivers tried to bypass flooded roads, including what he believes was Savona Boulevard. Camarda said he had never seen flooding on his own street before, though he has watched water pool near Oak Hammock a couple of times in the past. He said city crews used to clean the swale in front of his home about once a month, but he believes that has stopped. "I've been waiting for these guys to clean up. I haven't seen them," Camarda said.

City spokesperson Scott Samples said the rain came in faster than the stormwater system could handle, with canals, swales and retention ponds already full before the storm hit. At one location the city monitored, he said, about two feet of water arrived in roughly 30 minutes. Samples said water had receded from most roadways by about 8:30 p.m. Tuesday, which he described as the stormwater system working as designed. He said Public Works checks drainage before heavy rain and works to keep swales, drains and canals clear, but there is only so much crews can do when that much water arrives at once. He added that residents who cannot get home should find another place to stay if possible, and that the city is working closely with police on safety.

The city's capital plan for fiscal years 2027 through 2031, submitted to City Council on April 13, includes the Oak Hammock Watershed Improvement Project, budgeted at $8 million in each of the first two years and $7 million in each of the next two, for $30 million total, funded through stormwater bond financing. The project would add retention ponds, pump systems and upgraded valves in the California Boulevard area, covering territory east of Interstate 95, north of the C-23 Canal and Port St. Lucie Boulevard, and west of Florida's Turnpike. Samples said the city has just begun early data analysis that will guide the design, which could include new retention ponds, canal pumps, or raising the roadway at California and Savona boulevards so water drains off. He said it is too early to predict when construction will start, since the city must first gather data, finalize a design and secure funding, but called Oak Hammock a priority. "It will move as fast as it possibly can," Samples said. Part of the funding would come from a proposed $6 increase in the annual stormwater assessment, raising it from $183 to $189, which the city says would also support drainage work at the Elkcam Basin, the E-8 Canal and Hogpen Slough, along with faster replacement of swales and culverts. The city maintains about 200 miles of canals, 1,200 miles of swales and more than 6,000 culverts, though it notes that maintaining swales and driveway culverts between the pavement and the property line is the responsibility of individual property owners under city code.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Shooting Suspects Face Attempted Homicide, Accessory Charges
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce Police have formally charged two 18-year-olds arrested in last weekend's South Sixth Street shooting, which erupted from a domestic dispute. Keibin Lopez-Godoy faces a first-degree attempted homicide charge, while Kailee Yurubi faces an accessory after the fact charge.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce Police have filed formal charges against two 18-year-olds arrested in connection with a shooting last weekend that began as a domestic dispute on South Sixth Street. Keibin Lopez-Godoy faces a charge of first-degree attempted homicide, and Kailee Yurubi faces a charge of accessory after the fact, according to the Fort Pierce Police Department.

The case stems from an incident on Saturday, October 3, when officers responded to South Sixth Street at 7:12 a.m. after a woman called police to report that someone was shooting at her. Police said the woman had gone to the address to speak with her boyfriend about their relationship. When she arrived, several people ran out of the residence and attacked her.

The woman managed to escape the attack, get into her vehicle and drive away, police said. As she fled, one of the suspects grabbed a gun from the property and opened fire on her vehicle, according to investigators.

Police said a second person was arrested for allegedly driving the shooter away from the scene afterward. Lopez-Godoy and Yurubi were both taken into custody and now face their respective charges in the case.

cards.headline: Five Years Later, Port St. Lucie Police Still Seek Tips in Gabriella Hanley Shooting Death
cards.teaser: Gabriella Hanley, 20, was killed when gunmen fired 37 rounds into her car on Southeast Green River Parkway in 2021. No one has been charged, and police are renewing their call for tips.
cards.body:
Five years after 20-year-old Gabriella Hanley was shot and killed in Port St. Lucie, no one has been charged in her death, and police are asking anyone with information to come forward. Port St. Lucie police said detectives have continued investigating the case through interviews, forensic and digital evidence, and investigative leads, but the shooting remains unsolved.

The attack happened on Oct. 5, 2021, around 11:45 p.m. near Southeast Green River Parkway and Southeast Charleston Drive. Police said Hanley was driving a black Kia Forte southbound on Southeast Green River Parkway with her boyfriend, 21-year-old Darrick Mincey Jr., when another vehicle pulled alongside them and opened fire. Hanley was shot multiple times. Officers and rescue personnel attempted lifesaving measures at the scene, but she died in the early morning hours that followed. Mincey was also struck by gunfire but survived.

Investigators determined the Kia had sustained 37 bullet impacts. Numerous 9mm cartridge casings recovered from the scene were later found through forensic examination to have been fired from two different firearms, police said. The suspect vehicle was described as a silver four-door sedan that fled southbound on Southeast Green River Parkway after the shooting.

As of Tuesday, five years after the attack, no arrests have been made. Port St. Lucie police are asking anyone with information about what happened to Hanley that night, no matter how small it may seem, to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department Major Crimes Division at 772-871-5000 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS (8477). Tips can remain anonymous.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Precincts 39, 52 Move to Lakewood Park Church for Nov. 3 Vote
cards.teaser: Voters in Precincts 39 and 52 will cast ballots at a new location this fall after renovations forced a change from their usual clubhouse site. The Supervisor of Elections is urging early voting to avoid Election Day lines.
cards.body:
Voters in St. Lucie County's Precincts 39 and 52 will use a temporary polling place for the Nov. 3 general election because of renovations at their regular site. Supervisor of Elections Gertrude Walker announced Tuesday that voters in both precincts will move from the Spanish Lakes Country Club clubhouse to Lakewood Park Church, 5405 Turnpike Feeder Road in Fort Pierce.

Walker encouraged affected voters, along with the rest of the county's electorate, to consider early voting to avoid confusion or long lines on Election Day. Early voting hours run until 6 p.m. at eight sites across the county, including the county's newest early voting location, the Lakewood Park Branch Library at 7605 Santa Barbara Drive in Fort Pierce.

Other early voting sites include the Renaissance Business Park at 4132 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce, the Zora Neale Hurston Library at 3008 Avenue D in Fort Pierce, and the MIDFlorida Credit Union Event Center at 9221 SE Event Center Place in Port St. Lucie. Additional locations include the Community Center at 2195 SE Airoso Blvd., the Lewis Library at 2950 Rosser Blvd., the Indian River State College Veterans Center of Excellence at 500 NW California Blvd., and the Minsky Gym at 750 SW Darwin Blvd., all in Port St. Lucie.

Voters who prefer to vote by mail must request their ballots by the county's deadline in October. Walker's office recommends returning mailed ballots at least seven days before Election Day to ensure timely delivery. Completed ballots can also be dropped off at any early voting site or at designated Supervisor of Elections locations, including the Renaissance Business Park in Fort Pierce, the St. Lucie West South County Annex at 250 NW Country Club Drive, the Conrad Administration Annex at 1664 SE Walton Road, and the Tradition Tax Collector office at 10264 SW Village Parkway, all in Port St. Lucie.

hero.headline: DeSantis declares emergency in 25 North Florida counties as Tropical Depression Nine looms
hero.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed an executive order Tuesday declaring a state of emergency for 25 Florida counties as Tropical Depression Nine threatens to strengthen and move toward the state later this week. The order covers Baker, Bay, Calhoun, Columbia, Dixie, Escambia, Franklin, Gadsden, Gilchrist, Gulf, Hamilton, Holmes, Jackson, Jefferson, Lafayette, Leon, Liberty, Madison, Okaloosa, Santa Rosa, Suwannee, Taylor, Walton, Wakulla and Washington counties.

"Today, I signed an Executive Order issuing a state of emergency ahead of potential impacts from Tropical Depression 9. This order will allow the Florida Division of Emergency Management to stage critical preparedness resources and ensure Florida is ready to respond," DeSantis said.

The current forecast indicates a tropical storm or hurricane could make landfall somewhere along the central Gulf Coast later this week, according to a Tuesday statement from the governor's office. Impacts are expected to extend well beyond the landfall location, with heavy rainfall, strong winds, coastal flooding and isolated tornadoes possible across North Florida. The statement warned that additional rain could further saturate soils already soaked by the state's recent significant rainfall, raising the risk of flash flooding.

DeSantis urged Floridians statewide to finalize disaster plans and check their hurricane supplies ahead of the storm's arrival. The executive order allows state emergency management officials to begin staging resources in advance of any landfall, as forecasters continue to track the storm's path and potential for strengthening.

hero.headline: 5 Years After Gabriella Hanley's Killing on Green River Parkway, Case Remains Unsolved
hero.body:
Five years after Gabriella "Gabi" Hanley was shot and killed in an apparent drive-by shooting along Green River Parkway in Port St. Lucie, no arrests have been made in her case. Hanley was 20 years old when she was shot in 2021. Her boyfriend, who was in the car with her at the time, was also hit by gunfire but survived. Port St. Lucie police identified several people of interest in the case at the time of the shooting, but five years later no one has been arrested.

Hanley left behind a daughter who was 14 months old at the time of the shooting and is now 6 years old. The pain of losing Gabi still lingers for her mother, Nicole Vigilante. "It is tough, but I gotta be strong for my granddaughter," Vigilante said. As Gabi's daughter grows older, the family is searching for answers for themselves and for her. "Now she's getting older, and she has questions," Vigilante said. "And we want to be able to give her those answers," added Krystal Benitez, Gabi's cousin.

For Gabi's loved ones, her daughter is a constant reminder of who she was. "We're reminded of the situation every single day," said Alexia Perez, Gabi's best friend. "We will never forget Gabi. Her daughter is walking memory of her." Benitez called Gabi "an amazing, amazing woman."

Port St. Lucie police turned to social media Tuesday, saying information that was not shared at the time of the shooting could make a difference today. The department is asking anyone with information to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department's Major Crimes Division at 772-871-5000 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-8477.

Gabi's family and friends are doing their part to keep the case alive by sharing her story and raising awareness throughout the community. "We have been spending the day handing out flyers going to all local businesses just trying to again raise awareness," Benitez said. They are now calling on the community to come forward with information. "There's a little girl right now that's being raised without her mother, so be brave for her and come forward," Benitez said.

cards.headline: Murder Suspect Michael Waggle Extradited to Indian River County Jail
cards.teaser: Michael A. Waggle, wanted in the killing of Dawn M. Kriskewic in Vero Beach, was booked into the Indian River County Jail after being captured in West Virginia. He now faces a first-degree murder charge without bail.
cards.body:
Michael A. Waggle, the man accused of shooting and killing Dawn M. Kriskewic in Vero Beach, has been extradited back to Indian River County and booked into the Indian River County Jail on a first-degree murder charge. The Indian River County Sheriff's Office jail database shows Waggle, 33, was booked into the jail on Monday, Oct. 5.

According to the sheriff's office, Waggle and Kriskewic were in some sort of a relationship at the time of the shooting. After the killing, Waggle fled the area and was eventually captured at a motel in Dunbar, West Virginia, on Aug. 25.

Court documents indicate Waggle was later transferred to the Mecklenburg County Sheriff's Office in Charlotte, North Carolina, on Sept. 10. Indian River County Sheriff's Office personnel traveled to Charlotte to retrieve Waggle and bring him back to Indian River County to face charges.

Waggle is being held in the Indian River County Jail in Vero Beach without bail as he faces the first-degree murder charge in Kriskewic's death.

hero.headline: Five Years Later, Port St. Lucie Police Still Seek Tips in Gabriella Hanley Shooting Death
hero.teaser: Gabriella Hanley, 20, was killed in a drive-by shooting on Southeast Green River Parkway in Port St. Lucie five years ago this week, and no one has ever been charged. Police are renewing their appeal for public tips as the investigation continues.
hero.body:
Five years after 20-year-old Gabriella Hanley was shot and killed in a drive-by shooting in Port St. Lucie, no one has been charged in her death, and police are asking anyone with information to come forward. The shooting happened on Oct. 5, 2021, around 11:45 p.m. near Southeast Green River Parkway and Southeast Charleston Drive, according to Port St. Lucie police.

Police said Hanley was driving southbound on Southeast Green River Parkway in a black Kia Forte with her boyfriend, 21-year-old Darrick Mincey Jr., when another vehicle pulled alongside them and opened fire. Hanley was shot multiple times. Officers and rescue personnel attempted lifesaving measures at the scene, but she died in the early morning hours that followed. Mincey was also struck by gunfire but survived.

Investigators determined the Kia sustained 37 bullet impacts during the shooting. Numerous 9mm cartridge casings were recovered from the scene, and forensic examination showed they were fired from two different firearms, according to police. The suspect vehicle was described as a silver four-door sedan that fled southbound on Southeast Green River Parkway.

Port St. Lucie Police Department detectives have continued investigating Hanley's death in the years since, conducting numerous interviews, examining forensic and digital evidence, and following up on investigative leads. As of Tuesday, no arrests have been made. Police are urging anyone with information about what happened that night, no matter how small it may seem, to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department's Major Crimes Division at 772-871-5000 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-800-273-TIPS (8477). Tips can be submitted anonymously.

hero.headline: Flowers: Video Shows Teen Punching Into Truck Before Fatal Shooting at Garcia's Boat Ramp
hero.body:
Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said video evidence shows the 17-year-old killed Friday night at Garcia's Boat Ramp was throwing punches into a truck moments before he was shot, as investigators continue examining whether the shooting was an act of self-defense. The shooting happened during a confrontation at the popular waterfront spot, which authorities say has become a frequent gathering place for teens.

Flowers said investigators reviewed video showing the teen open the door of a truck and begin punching people inside just before a shot was fired. "The 17-year-old opens the door, and he starts to punch. He's going to punch the people that are inside of that truck," Flowers said during a news conference. "That shot is the shot that ultimately killed the 17-year-old in this case." The Indian River County Sheriff's Office released video showing the confrontation in the moments before the shooting.

Both the shooter and the driver of the truck have cooperated with investigators, turning over the firearm and the vehicle involved in the incident. As of Monday, no arrests had been made. "It's gonna be up to the state on whether charges are ultimately filed, but I can tell you, self-defense plays a part in these," Flowers said. The investigation remains active, and the sheriff is asking anyone with video footage or information about the shooting, or about future teen meetup events, to contact investigators.

Flowers also addressed the role social media has played in drawing large groups of teenagers to locations like Garcia's Boat Ramp, warning that the presence of firearms at these gatherings is raising the stakes. "We got kids out here losing their lives chasing likes and shares on social media," Flowers said. cards.headline: New I-95 Oslo Road Interchange Opens Early in Indian River County
cards.teaser: The $100 million interchange opened about a year ahead of schedule and is the first new I-95 interchange built in Indian River County in nearly 50 years.
cards.body:
Governor Ron DeSantis visited Indian River County on Monday to celebrate the completion of a new I-95 interchange at Oslo Road, a $100 million project state officials say will improve traffic flow, emergency response times and freight movement. The interchange opened about a year ahead of schedule and marks the first new I-95 interchange built in Indian River County in nearly 50 years.

DeSantis said the project provides a new direct connection to I-95 for southern Indian River County while easing congestion at nearby interchanges at Indrio Road and State Road 60. "This is going to bring a new critical connection to I-95 for a part of the state that has changed quite a bit," DeSantis said. The governor said drivers using Oslo Road to access I-95 can expect travel times to be cut roughly in half, and state transportation officials project traffic along the corridor will keep growing through 2045.

DeSantis said the project is also expected to deliver major public safety benefits. The state estimates emergency response times in the area could drop by as much as 56%, letting first responders reach crashes and other emergencies more quickly. "This will ultimately save some lives because time is of the essence in some of these situations," DeSantis said. Florida Department of Transportation Secretary Jared Perdue said faster access to I-95 for first responders is one of the project's most important features. "Every single second counts when it comes to saving lives, and this is going to reduce the time it takes for first responders to get to incidents substantially," Perdue said. The interchange is also expected to improve freight movement for businesses in southern Indian River County by giving trucks and commercial traffic a more direct route to the interstate.

State officials said the project was accelerated through Florida's Moving Florida Forward initiative, a transportation funding program launched by the DeSantis administration to speed up major road projects statewide. Perdue said FDOT worked with contractors through a "voluntary acceleration" program that rewarded construction teams for finishing work faster, and the Oslo Road interchange was completed approximately 400 days ahead of schedule. FDOT also acquired land near the interchange to establish a dedicated gopher tortoise habitat, which state officials said will serve as the only relocation site of its kind in Southeast Florida, allowing protected tortoises to be moved while infrastructure work continues. The Oslo Road interchange is part of nearly $1 billion in planned transportation investments across the Treasure Coast. "This interchange sets a clear example of how Florida delivers infrastructure that improves quality of life today while building more capacity for the future," DeSantis said.

hero.headline: Sheriff: Video Shows Teen Punching Into Truck Before Fatal Garcia's Boat Ramp Shooting
hero.body:
Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said video footage shows a 17-year-old throwing punches into a truck moments before he was fatally shot Friday night at Garcia's Boat Ramp, and investigators are weighing whether the shooting was an act of self-defense. No arrests have been made as of Monday, and Flowers said it will ultimately be up to the state attorney's office to decide whether charges are filed.

The shooting happened during a confrontation at the waterfront site, which authorities say has become a popular meetup spot for teenagers. Flowers said investigators reviewed video showing the teen open the door of a truck and begin punching people inside. "The 17-year-old opens the door, and he starts to punch. He's going to punch the people that are inside of that truck," Flowers said during a news conference. "That shot is the shot that ultimately killed the 17-year-old in this case." The Indian River County Sheriff's Office released video of the confrontation that led up to the shooting.

Both the shooter and the driver of the truck have cooperated with investigators, turning over the firearm and the vehicle involved in the incident, according to the sheriff's office. Flowers said self-defense is a factor under consideration in the case. "It's gonna be up to the state on whether charges are ultimately filed, but I can tell you, self-defense plays a part in these," he said.

Flowers tied the shooting to a broader pattern of large teen gatherings organized through social media at locations like Garcia's Boat Ramp, warning that firearms are raising the stakes of those meetups. "We got kids out here losing their lives chasing likes and shares on social media," Flowers said. "Now we're adding guns into the mix, and we're adding social media into the mix, and so what we're seeing is an escalation of each one of these." He urged parents to know where their children are and suggested location-tracking tools as a safety measure. The investigation remains active, and the sheriff's office is asking anyone with video footage or information about the shooting, or about future teen meetup events, to contact investigators.

hero.headline: Florida Terminates 220+ Medicaid Providers, Projects $1 Billion in Savings
hero.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis announced Tuesday that Florida has terminated more than 220 Medicaid providers for fraud, waste or abuse, part of an enforcement push the state says has produced more than $1 billion in projected savings. DeSantis spoke at the Healthcare District of Palm Beach County alongside Agency for Health Care Administration Secretary Shevaun Harris, detailing an expanded effort to root out fraudulent billing and improper payments in the state Medicaid program.

"We want to make sure that what is being spent is being spent well," DeSantis said. "Medicaid dollars must go to healthcare for eligible Floridians, not to people who are gaming the system." State officials said AHCA has conducted more than 400 provider site visits since January, relying on expanded data analytics, claims monitoring and background screening to flag suspicious activity. More than 150 fraud-related referrals have gone to the Florida Attorney General's Office over the past year, and more than 250 providers have been placed on payment restrictions or had payments suspended. The terminated providers accounted for more than $230 million in Medicaid billing in 2025, according to state officials.

A central focus of the crackdown has been Applied Behavioral Analysis services, which are commonly used to treat children with autism. Harris said Florida Medicaid spent approximately $6.57 billion on ABA services between 2023 and 2025, nearly four times more than any other state's Medicaid program, with spending at one point projected to grow 30% annually. Investigators found providers billing for implausible service schedules, including claims for more than 24 hours of care in a single day and services supposedly delivered continuously through weekends and holidays. The state moved ABA services into managed care in 2025, a shift officials say has strengthened oversight and slowed spending growth to under 10% annually, lowering projected ABA expenditures to roughly $2.8 billion, more than $1 billion below earlier forecasts. "That is where we want our funding going," Harris said. "Not in the pockets of crooks."

AHCA has also partnered with identity verification company SentiLink to screen providers before they enter the Medicaid system, aiming to catch synthetic identities and suspicious ownership structures early. DeSantis and Harris said the enforcement effort targets fraudulent providers, not the families who depend on Medicaid-funded services, including those seeking ABA therapy for children with autism. Asked about families in Palm Beach County struggling to access ABA therapy after providers were removed, Harris said managed care plans are working to connect affected recipients with new providers. "If there is a parent watching and they're having any issues, they can contact the agency and we will help them ourselves or connect them with their managed care plan," Harris said.

DeSantis framed the Medicaid enforcement push as part of a broader push for fiscal responsibility, pointing to recent state budget reductions, debt repayment and tax relief measures. He said AHCA will keep conducting site visits, monitoring claims and referring suspected fraud for investigation. "This is kind of just the opening salvo," DeSantis said. "I would anticipate you will see more results coming in the weeks, months and years ahead."

hero.headline: Murder Suspect Michael Waggle Extradited to Indian River County Jail
hero.teaser: Michael Waggle, wanted in the killing of Dawn Kriskewic, has been returned to Indian River County and booked into the jail without bail.
hero.body:
A man wanted in connection with a Vero Beach murder has been returned to Indian River County. According to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office jail database, Michael A. Waggle, 33, was booked into the jail on Monday, Oct. 5.

Waggle is accused of shooting and killing Dawn M. Kriskewic. The sheriff's office said Waggle and Kriskewic were in some sort of relationship. After the shooting, Waggle fled the area and was captured at a motel in Dunbar, West Virginia, on Aug. 28.

Court documents show Waggle was later transferred to the Mecklenburg County Sheriff's Office in Charlotte, North Carolina, in September. Indian River County Sheriff's Office personnel traveled there to retrieve him and bring him back to Vero Beach. Waggle faces a first-degree murder charge and is being held in the Indian River County Jail without bail.

hero.headline: Sheriff: Self-Defense a Factor in Teen's Fatal Shooting at Garcia's Boat Ramp
hero.body:
A 17-year-old was shot and killed Friday night during a confrontation at Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County, and investigators are examining whether the shooting was an act of self-defense, according to Sheriff Eric Flowers. As of Monday, no arrests had been made in the case.

Flowers said the boat ramp has become a frequent gathering spot for teenagers, and video reviewed by investigators showed the 17-year-old opening the door of a truck and throwing punches at people inside before a shot was fired. "The 17-year-old opens the door, and he starts to punch. He's going to punch the people that are inside of that truck," Flowers said during a news conference. "That shot is the shot that ultimately killed the 17-year-old in this case." The Indian River County Sheriff's Office released video showing the confrontation moments before the shooting.

Authorities said both the shooter and the driver of the truck have cooperated with investigators, turning over the firearm and the vehicle involved in the incident. Flowers said it will be up to the state to decide whether charges are filed. "It's gonna be up to the state on whether charges are ultimately filed, but I can tell you, self-defense plays a part in these," he said.

Flowers linked the shooting to a broader pattern of large teen gatherings organized through social media at locations like Garcia's Boat Ramp, warning that the presence of firearms is raising the stakes of those meetups. "We got kids out here losing their lives chasing likes and shares on social media," Flowers said. "Now we're adding guns into the mix, and we're adding social media into the mix, and so what we're seeing is an escalation of each one of these." The investigation remains active, and the sheriff is asking anyone with video footage or information about the shooting, or about future teen meetup events, to contact investigators. Flowers also urged parents to know where their children are and suggested location-tracking tools as one way to help keep them safe.

hero.headline: New I-95 Interchange at Oslo Road Opens a Year Early in Indian River County
hero.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis opened a new I-95 interchange at Oslo Road in Indian River County on Monday, marking the completion of a roughly $100 million project finished a full year ahead of schedule. DeSantis called it a critical new connection for drivers, emergency crews and the region's growing population, and said it is the first new interchange built in this part of the state in almost 50 years.

DeSantis said the new exit is expected to ease congestion at the nearby Indrio Road and State Road 60 interchanges. Drivers traveling from Oslo Road to I-95 can expect their travel times to be cut in half, he said. With daily traffic on the corridor projected to keep growing through 2045, DeSantis said the project shows how the state can improve quality of life now while building capacity for the future.

The governor said the direct interstate connection will also speed up emergency response in southern Indian River County. "We anticipate that just for the local community on a normal basis, for local, like non-hurricane-type emergencies, that the emergency response time will be reduced by up to 56%," DeSantis said. "That will ultimately save some lives, of course, because time is of the essence in some of these situations." Florida Department of Transportation Secretary Jared Perdue said the project was completed 400 days early through what the agency calls voluntary acceleration, a process that lets contractors propose ways to speed up construction in exchange for sharing in the savings. "This is going to reduce the time it takes for first responders to get to incidents substantially," Perdue said. "We're really excited about that, to include cutting commute time in half and so many other benefits." Perdue also said nearly $1 billion in transportation investment is planned for the Treasure Coast region.

DeSantis said FDOT acquired nearby land for a dedicated gopher tortoise habitat, which he said will be the only relocation site of its kind in Southeast Florida. "Florida [is] showing that it's possible to do the projects that we need done while also buttressing environmental stewardship," DeSantis said. Indian River County Commissioner Joseph Flescher recalled his surprise at how quickly the project came together. "When I got the phone call, I said, 'We're not near completion. I had been here just two weeks ago. We were nowhere near where we're at,'" Flescher said. "This team worked an incredible operation." Flescher said the interchange addresses needs tied to the county's current growth, not just its future. "This interchange is very much needed in the development of our county," he said. "And I don't mean the future development. I mean the current development."

hero.headline: State Says No Elevated Brain Cancer Rates in St. Lucie County; Mast Presses CDC
hero.body:
The Florida Department of Health's St. Lucie County Health Officer Clint Sperber says an updated review of cancer registry data through 2023 shows no sign of elevated brain cancer rates in the county, even as families continue to track new diagnoses, including three confirmed in August alone. The finding comes as Rep. Brian Mast renews his call for the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to examine the underlying data behind state conclusions.

"Our latest analysis, which includes data through 2023, shows no indication of higher rates in St. Lucie County or in the specific zip codes people have asked about," Sperber wrote, adding that the county's rates are in line with nearby counties and the state as a whole. The updated report was not available when he responded, and he said officials were finishing a summary to release online. His response did not explain how the analysis handled tumors initially classified as one type and later diagnosed as glioblastoma, or whether other brain cancers were examined separately. It also did not specify what would trigger additional environmental testing. A 2019 state review had examined glioblastoma diagnoses from 1998 through 2017 in ZIP codes 34952, 34982 and 34983, finding no statistically significant increase and no designated cancer cluster, but that review did not include later diagnoses or the broader range of brain tumors families are now tracking.

Stephanie Ankiel, who helps patients through the Brain Cancer Foundation of the Treasure Coast, has spent years mapping where patients lived in search of possible connections. Driving through Fort Pierce, she pointed to her late husband's childhood home and, a few houses away, a home where she said a resident was diagnosed in 2025 with the same type of brain tumor her husband, Mark Cunningham, first had: oligodendroglioma, which later progressed to glioblastoma. A few streets away, she identified a home where she said two unrelated residents developed glioblastoma 20 years apart, and elsewhere along the route she pointed to neighboring homes where she said a woman and an 18-year-old had been diagnosed with brain cancer. Ankiel wants officials to examine the full range of brain cancers on her map, not just glioblastoma. The diagnoses and proximity of patients' homes do not establish a cancer cluster or a common cause, and no environmental factor questioned by families has been established as a cause.

Mast said he has again asked the CDC to examine the concerns and provide the data behind its conclusions. "You need to give us the receipts," Mast said. "Give us the data of where these took place, how many of them took place." The CDC said state and local health departments lead examinations of unusual cancer patterns and confirmed it assisted Florida's investigation in 2018, but it did not address whether it had received Mast's latest request or would open a new review. A CDC spokesperson said the agency "is prepared to provide additional assistance upon the Florida Department of Health's request."

Matt Elliott, diagnosed this year with glioblastoma, said he initially believed his case was isolated until he met other local patients. "I thought I was the only one," he said. He has decided not to continue treatment and is instead spending his time with friends and family, going to the beach and swimming. "It might take them years to even figure out what the hell's going on around here," Elliott said. "I can't expect myself to be around at the end of it." He said he wants investigators to find answers but is focused on the life he has left. "I'm not going to be that person that lives to be 65, 70, 80 years old," Elliott said. "But I get to hang out with my friends. I get to go take a swim, have some fun."

cards.headline: St. Lucie Precincts 39 and 52 Get New Polling Site for Nov. 3 Election
cards.teaser: Voters in two St. Lucie County precincts will cast ballots at a new location after renovations closed their usual polling place. Supervisor of Elections Gertrude Walker is also urging residents to use early voting to avoid Election Day lines.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County voters assigned to Precincts 39 and 52 will vote at a temporary polling place for the Nov. 3 general election because of renovations at their usual site. Supervisor of Elections Gertrude Walker announced Tuesday that voters in the two precincts will move from the Spanish Lakes Country Club clubhouse to Lakewood Park Church, 5405 Turnpike Feeder Road in Fort Pierce.

Walker encouraged voters to take advantage of early voting, including at the county's newest early voting site, Lakewood Park Branch Library, 7605 Santa Barbara Drive in Fort Pierce, to avoid lines on Election Day. Early voting hours run until 6 p.m. at locations across the county, including the Renaissance Business Park at 4132 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce, the Zora Neale Hurston Library at 3008 Avenue D in Fort Pierce, the MIDFlorida Credit Union Event Center at 9221 SE Event Center Place in Port St. Lucie, the Community Center at 2195 SE Airoso Blvd. in Port St. Lucie, the Lewis Library at 2950 Rosser Blvd. in Port St. Lucie, the Indian River State College Veterans Center of Excellence at 500 NW California Blvd. in Port St. Lucie and Minsky Gym at 750 SW Darwin Blvd. in Port St. Lucie.

Voters who want to cast a ballot by mail must request one by the deadline set by the Supervisor of Elections office. Walker's office is encouraging anyone returning a ballot by mail to do so at least seven days before Election Day to ensure it arrives in time to be counted.

Vote-by-mail ballots can also be dropped off in person at any early voting site or at designated Supervisor of Elections locations, including the Renaissance Business Park at 4132 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce, the St. Lucie West South County Annex at 250 NW Country Club Drive in Port St. Lucie, the Conrad Administration Annex at 1664 SE Walton Road in Port St. Lucie and the Tradition Tax Collector office at 10264 SW Village Parkway in Port St. Lucie. Voters with questions about their assigned precinct or the location changes can contact the Supervisor of Elections office ahead of the Nov. 3 election.

hero.headline: Sheriff Flowers Investigates If Teen's Fatal Shooting at Garcia's Boat Ramp Was Self-Defense
hero.body:
Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said investigators are examining whether the fatal shooting of a 17-year-old Friday night at Garcia's Boat Ramp was an act of self-defense. The shooting happened during a confrontation at the waterfront spot, which authorities say has become a popular meetup location for teenagers.

Flowers said investigators reviewed video showing the 17-year-old open the door of a truck and throw punches at people inside before a shot was fired. "The 17-year-old opens the door, and he starts to punch. He's going to punch the people that are inside of that truck," Flowers said during a news conference. "That shot is the shot that ultimately killed the 17-year-old in this case." The Indian River County Sheriff's Office released video of the confrontation moments before the shooting.

Both the shooter and the driver of the truck have cooperated with investigators, turning over the firearm and vehicle involved, according to authorities. As of Monday, no arrests had been made. "It's gonna be up to the state on whether charges are ultimately filed, but I can tell you, self-defense plays a part in these," Flowers said. The investigation remains active, and the sheriff is asking anyone with video footage or information about the shooting, or about future teen meetup events, to contact investigators.

Flowers said social media has played a role in drawing large groups of teenagers to locations like Garcia's Boat Ramp and warned that the presence of firearms is raising the risks tied to those gatherings. "We got kids out here losing their lives chasing likes and shares on social media," Flowers said. "Now we're adding guns into the mix, and we're adding social media into the mix, and so what we're seeing is an escalation of each one of these." Flowers also urged parents to know where their children are and suggested location-tracking tools as one way to help keep them safe.

hero.headline: Fellsmere Teen Meetup Shooting Leaves Sebastian River Student Dead, Sheriff Cites Self-Defense Claim
hero.teaser: Sulliman Bah, 17, died after a gathering of more than 100 teens at Garcia's Boat Ramp turned violent. Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers says a self-defense claim may apply.
hero.body:
A 17-year-old has been identified as the teen killed in a shooting Friday night at Garcia's Boat Ramp in Fellsmere, where a meetup of more than 100 teens turned violent. Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said the gathering included teens ages 14 to 19, with drinking and fighting reported before the shooting around 11:24 p.m. The family confirmed the victim was Sulliman Bah, a senior at Sebastian River High School who had recently withdrawn from the school to be home schooled, according to a district spokesperson.

According to detectives, Bah and a group of friends approached a pickup truck occupied by two 18-year-olds. Bah opened the truck door and attempted to punch someone inside when the passenger fired a single shot, striking him. Friends carried Bah toward Fellsmere, where deputies and EMS met them at Fellsmere City Hall and performed CPR. He was taken first to Sebastian River Medical Center, then transported to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he died from his injuries.

No arrests have been made. Flowers said the driver and passenger from the truck have cooperated with investigators, turning over the truck and the firearm used in the shooting. Investigators used Flock technology to identify people connected to the vehicle and the shooting, and deputies recovered additional guns and multiple shell casings at the scene. The sheriff said the preliminary investigation points toward a self-defense claim. "We will be submitting a warrant in the case, but at this time it looks as though there will be a self-defense claim as a result," Flowers said, adding that the State Attorney's Office will ultimately decide whether charges are filed. Flowers said there may have been as many as four fights at the boat ramp that night and that the group involved had "a history of fighting," calling it "an ongoing thing."

Flowers said the meetup reflects a growing trend of teens gathering at remote locations arranged through Snapchat, where fights are recorded and shared online. "We got kids out here losing their lives chasing likes and shares on social media," he said. "We've got kids out here losing their lives trying to go viral on social media." He warned that combining guns with teen gatherings is dangerous, saying, "It's not safe. There's guns, and those two just don't mix. And now add in the fuel of the fire of social media, and now we have a 17-year-old dead." Flowers urged parents to ask their children whether they attended the meetup and asked anyone who witnessed or recorded the shooting to contact investigators. The School District of Indian River County said it is "heartbroken" by Bah's death and had grief counselors available over the weekend, including at Sebastian River High School's Homecoming Dance, with support continuing as students and staff returned to school.

Indian River County Fire Rescue personnel pronounced the box truck driver dead at the scene at 4:46 p.m. from injuries suffered in the collision.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Woman Pleads Guilty in Palm Beach County Apartment Theft Scheme
hero.body:
A Port St. Lucie woman pleaded guilty Monday to stealing tens of thousands of dollars from residents of a Palm Beach County apartment complex while working as their community manager. Ashley R. Clayton, 38, entered a guilty plea on Oct. 5 to money laundering, organized scheme to defraud and making false entry in book of business entity, according to Palm Beach County court documents. Clayton agreed to the plea deal on Sept. 28.

Clayton was sentenced to five years of probation on each charge, to be served concurrently. She was credited with 12 days already served in Palm Beach County jail and ordered to pay court costs and complete community service. She must also undergo mental health and substance abuse evaluations and is banned from handling any financial transactions for a business or another person. Under the plea agreement, Clayton and the victim will work out how much restitution she owes the property management company.

According to a Riviera Beach Police Department report, Clayton worked for three months as community manager at Berkeley Landing Apartments, located at 3100 Broadway, where she oversaw rent payments, deposits, application fees, background and credit checks, and the compliance application process. A regional manager for the complex told police on June 13, 2024, that Clayton had been directing residents to pay through Zelle, with the money going into her personal bank account. Some residents gave her blank money orders. Police said Clayton sent residents a letter on apartment complex letterhead telling them rent had to be paid by money order "until further notice" while payment ledgers were being updated, a letter the complex never authorized her to send.

After she was fired, Clayton returned to the property and handed over 20 money orders worth $14,798.22 to management, but police said she kept three others and tried to cash them at an Amscot in Miami. One was successfully cashed, leaving the complex short at least $11,999.23. Investigators determined Clayton collected $31,249.32 through Zelle transfers, bringing the total stolen to at least $58,046.77. The police report identified five additional people from whom Clayton took money under false pretenses while employed at the complex.

hero.headline: Mother of Teen Killed at Indian River Boat Ramp Disputes Self-Defense Claim
hero.body:
The mother of the 17-year-old boy killed during a shooting Friday night at Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County is disputing claims that the shooting was self-defense. Sulliman Bah died after being shot by a passenger in a white pickup truck during a party that drew about 1,000 teenagers to the boat ramp, just south of Fellsmere. Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said Monday that investigators are examining whether the shooting was justified, but Bah's mother says her son was trying to protect others, not attack anyone.

At a news conference Monday afternoon, Flowers showed two videos of the shooting from different angles. The footage begins with Bah approaching the truck. "Seventeen-year-old opens the door, and he starts to punch. He's going to punch on the people that are inside of that truck. One shot is fired," Flowers said. The sheriff said the shot came from the passenger seat and killed Bah. Flowers said Bah had a history with the two 18-year-olds inside the truck, including prior fights, and that the pair told investigators they had the gun for protection. "At this time, it looks as though there will be a self-defense claim," Flowers said.

Bah's mother rejects that account. In a text message to a reporter, she said, "Sulliman was a defender of his friends. Always protecting the underdog, and I believe he was trying to save the crowd from that gun that he knew was about to be used...He was there to protect his friends from the thugs that had previously threatened him and many others multiple times." She said she does not see her son throwing a punch in the video. "If anything, I believe he was attempting to push the gun away," she said.

The sheriff's office has not released the identities of the two 18-year-olds in the truck, but Flowers said they are cooperating with investigators. No arrests have been made. Flowers said prosecutors will ultimately decide whether charges are filed. "It's going to be up to the state on whether charges ultimately will be filed. But I can tell you self-defense plays a part in these," he said. The sheriff said the investigation remains active and asked anyone who attended the party at Garcia's Boat Ramp to contact his office.

"At this time, it looks as though there will be a self-defense claim," Flowers said. Bah’s mother, however, disputes the self-defense claim. Always protecting the underdog, and I believe he was trying to save the crowd from that gun that he knew was about to be used...He was there to protect his friends from the thugs that had previously threatened him and many others multiple times." hero.headline: IRC Sheriff: Video Shows Teen Punching Before Fatal Boat Ramp Shooting
hero.body:
A 17-year-old died in a shooting Friday night at Garcia's Boat Ramp in Indian River County, and the sheriff said Monday that investigators are examining whether the shooting was an act of self-defense. Sheriff Eric Flowers held a news conference Monday to release new details, including video evidence, in a case that remains under investigation with no arrests made.

Flowers said investigators reviewed video showing the 17-year-old opening the door of a truck and throwing punches at people inside just before a shot was fired. "The 17-year-old opens the door, and he starts to punch. He's going to punch the people that are inside of that truck," Flowers said. "That shot is the shot that ultimately killed the 17-year-old in this case." The Indian River County Sheriff's Office released video of the confrontation that occurred moments before the shooting.

Authorities said both the shooter and the driver of the truck have cooperated with investigators, turning over the firearm and the vehicle involved in the incident. Flowers said it will ultimately be up to the State Attorney's Office to decide whether charges are filed. "It's gonna be up to the state on whether charges are ultimately filed, but I can tell you, self-defense plays a part in these," he said.

Flowers said the shooting happened during a confrontation at Garcia's Boat Ramp, which has become a popular meetup spot for large groups of teenagers, often organized through social media. He warned that the combination of social media and firearms is making those gatherings more dangerous. "We got kids out here losing their lives chasing likes and shares on social media," Flowers said. "Now we're adding guns into the mix, and we're adding social media into the mix, and so what we're seeing is an escalation of each one of these." He urged parents to know where their children are and suggested location-tracking tools as a way to help keep them safe. The sheriff's office is asking anyone with video footage or information about the shooting, or about future teen meetup events, to contact investigators.
